title: Natural comparison of open module stalks under restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $V\subseteq W\subseteq X$ open, and $x\in V$. Let $B$ be the restriction functor on module sheaves from the slice site over $W$ to that over $V$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $S_V$ and $S_W$ be the open module stalk functors at $x$, with values in modules over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor]. There is a natural isomorphism $B\circ S_V\cong S_W$, natural in every module sheaf on the slice site over $W$. No finiteness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00A0, lemma-restrict (3), including its module-sheaf clause; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00A0, read 2026-10-13. This is step 3 of lem-sc-perfect-open-stalk-degreewise-shrink.

proof.text: Use the fully proved germ argument from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.RestrictionStalkExtensionIso locally as private helpers. Represent scalar and module elements by germs on a common intersection. The inverse open-immersion stalk map sends the scalar germ to the inverse section-map germ; Scheme.Modules.germ_restrictStalkNatIso_hom_app and PresheafOfModules.germ_smul then show that the additive restriction-stalk comparison is semilinear over the inverse stalk map. It is therefore linear after restriction of scalars along the stalk map. Its underlying additive map is invertible by Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso. Naturality follows from the naturality of that same additive isomorphism, evaluated on each stalk element.

Replace the inclusion X.homOfLE hVW by Scheme.Hom.copyBase with the explicit subtype inclusion as its point map; copyBase_eq proves equality with the original inclusion. This makes both images of x definitionally the original point x. Scheme.Hom.stalkMap_congr_hom, stalkMap_comp and homOfLE_ι identify the composite stalk-ring map with the map from X to V. ModuleCat.restrictScalarsComp' gives the associated natural isomorphism of scalar-restriction functors.

Apply Scheme.Modules.overMapCompOverEquiv to identify restriction on slice sites with the open-immersion restriction functor. Whisker this comparison with the stalk and scalar-restriction functors. Then use the scalar-composition isomorphism and whisker the natural linear stalk comparison from step 1 with restriction of scalars from W to X. Compose with functor associators. The resulting natural isomorphism has exactly the required source and target functors. The construction imposes no finiteness hypotheses, includes equal opens, and has no instance when the smaller open is empty.

def openModuleStalkRestrictionComparison
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (W V : X.Opens) (hVW : V ≤ W)
    (x : X) (hxW : x ∈ W) (hxV : x ∈ V) :
    SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (homOfLE hVW : V ⟶ W) ⋙ openModuleStalkFunctor X V ⟨x, hxV⟩ ≅
      openModuleStalkFunctor X W ⟨x, hxW⟩
